content: E numbers are numerical codes assigned to food additives and are commonly displayed on food labels across the European Union. These codes are based on the International Numbering System (INS) as established by the Codex Alimentarius committee. However, only a specific subset of INS additives is approved for use within the European Union, and these are denoted by the prefix E, which signifies Europe. For example, bicarbonate of soda is one such additive with an E number designation. E numbers are also present on food labels in other regions, including the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries, Australia, New Zealand, and Israel. Although still relatively uncommon, they are increasingly appearing on food packaging in North America, particularly in Canada. It is important to note that the classification of E numbers by numeric range does not always encompass all examples within a given category. Additionally, many chemicals, especially those within the E400–E499 range, serve multiple functional purposes.
